title: Streaming marshalling & backpressure sweep for pinned model variants and perf-profile publication
creator: Liam Chen
description: Goal: Verify that newly onboarded model variants (float/quantized, sequence-length tuned) behave correctly end-to-end for streaming responses that include one or more tool/function calls, and that published performance profiles for pinned versions accurately reflect observed streaming latency and resource characteristics. This ticket covers marshalling/serialization edge cases, backpressure and connection-resume semantics, multi-tool call interleaving inside a single stream, and automated publication of the resulting perf profiles to the Console and model catalog for version-pinned deployments. Deliverables: (1) extended test harness scenarios for streaming + tool calls, (2) compatibility cert run and checklist, (3) updated perf-profile publish job that records streaming tail-latency and tool-call overhead for pinned versions, (4) follow-up issues for any regressions. Scope excludes on-prem deployment networking (handled in separate private infra ticket).
acceptance_criteria: The extended harness runs deterministically against the new model variant and returns PASS for all streaming handshakes (normal, resume, reconnect).
Function/tool calls embedded mid-stream preserve argument fidelity (JSON round-trip) and ordering across reconnects/backpressure events.
No silent truncation or duplicate tool-call events when applying continuous batching and KV cache snapshots.

Published perf-profile for the pinned version includes median/95/99 tail latency for start-token, mid-stream tool-call round-trip, and end-token, and those numbers match CI-collected values within accepted variance thresholds.
Console shows the new pinned-version entry with runtime-2.4 profile and streaming-specific metrics within 30 minutes of the successful cert run.
Smoke API tests (SDK + REST) for streaming tool-calls pass against the canary routing policy for pinned model variants.
All changes have code review and at least one design/PM sign-off recorded in the ticket comments.
test_plan: Add scenarios to streaming harness: single tool call at start, tool call mid-sequence, multiple sequential tool calls, tool-call with large argument payload (>64KB), and tool-call triggered after KV cache warmup.
Simulate backpressure by artificially delaying TCP/TLS reads on the client and assert server preserves stream offsets and tool-call boundaries.
Run replay tests: capture golden session for each scenario and run 10x replay under jittered network to check idempotency and ordering.
Run perf-profile collection job in CI for pinned variant: collect token-level timing, GPU utilization, batch sizes, and tool-call RTTs over 1k requests and compute distribution metrics.
Cross-validate console publish: CI artifacts -> internal storage -> publish job -> Catalog -> Console entry and verify timestamps/metadata.
Manual exploratory: use SDK to attach a long-poll consumer, force reconnects, and verify client-side SDK reassembly APIs still return coherent function call objects.
Run security fuzz: send malformed JSON within tool-call payload and ensure graceful error (400) with no server crash.
implementation_notes: Primary changes: extend streaming conformance harness (tests/streaming_onboarded_harness.go), add tool-call interleaving fixtures, and a CI job step to run perf collection and publish a JSON perf-profile artifact to internal storage. Update makefile / CI pipeline to run the certification step for all pinned variants in runtime-2.4 matrix. Add metrics to the perf-publisher: streaming_start_latency_ms, tool_call_avg_rtt_ms, tool_call_99th_tail_ms, stream_end_latency_ms, batch_size_histogram. Ensure perf-publisher labels pinned_version and model_architecture. Use existing cert-report format but add a 'streaming' section. Keep behavioral changes behind a feature-flag: onboarding.streaming_cert_enabled = true.
risks: Discovery of model runtime behavior that violates streaming invariant (e.g., inconsistent token offsets after reconnect) may require model-side fixes and delay onboarding.
Perf-profile published values could be noisy for low-QPS models — need minimum sample size threshold before publish to avoid misleading Console entries.
Publishing pipeline bug could expose internal perf artifacts if ACLs are misconfigured — gate publishing with internal ACL checks and a dry-run option.
Large tool payloads may trigger different kernel paths and reveal quantization correctness issues not caught in existing evals.

qa_notes: When validating in staging, set onboarding.streaming_cert_enabled=true in stage config and deploy runtime-2.4 canary before running harness.
Use SDK test client v0.8.2+ (includes reconnect helper) for manual exploratory testing.
Collect logs with request_id and stream_session_id tags to correlate client reconnects with server events.
For perf verification, run at least 1k end-to-end requests per variant to stabilize 99th-percentile estimates.
